t: Knowledge Granularity Controller: a plain-language overview
title: Knowledge Granularity Controller: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Granularity Controller does and why archives need it. A knowledge granularity controller decides how much detail to show: the quick answer, the solid summary, or the full deep dive. The same knowledge exists at every level, from a one-liner up to the complete record. Readers turn the detail dial and the system serves the right slice — never too thin, never overwhelming.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Knowledge Granularity Controller works
title: How the Knowledge Granularity Controller works
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Granularity Controller does and why archives need it. Real controllers build a granularity ladder over each record: extractive or abstractive summarization produces the one-line and paragraph levels, section-aware chunking preserves the full level, and key-fact lists serve the in-between rungs. Retrieval systems use the ladder to match query intent — a 'quick fact' query gets the top rung, a research query gets the full text with its summary as an entry point. Each level is generated from the same source so the summary can never contradict the full record.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Knowledge Granularity Controller works: the deep tour
title: How the Knowledge Granularity Controller works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Granularity Controller does and why archives need it. Real controllers build a granularity ladder over each record: extractive or abstractive summarization produces the one-line and paragraph levels, section-aware chunking preserves the full level, and key-fact lists serve the in-between rungs. Retrieval systems use the ladder to match query intent — a 'quick fact' query gets the top rung, a research query gets the full text with its summary as an entry point. Each level is generated from the same source so the summary can never contradict the full record. Advanced controllers pick the level per user and per task, track which levels actually get read to tune the ladder, and guarantee consistency: every claim in a summary must trace to a sentence in the full record. Quality is measured by summary faithfulness (no invented claims) and by task success at each level. The limits are topics where the 'simple version' would mislead — those carry a minimum-detail floor, because some ideas cannot be honestly compressed past a point.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
